CHAPTER 01 / WEBFRONT

Starting with C++

Building an application with WebFront: the C++ model and development stages.

Notation conventions

Function names, types, commands, options and filenames appear in monospace, for example describe, wf test or main.cpp. Italics introduce a term at its definition. Code blocks give the fragments to enter; the preceding text states their location and prerequisites.

Developing an application ↓The example programme ↓Building the examples ↓Running the simulation ↓

Developing an application

WebFront supports the creation of graphical applications and provides tools for their development. The C++ application, its presentation and its tests are developed together. The integrated environment then supports their evolution and prepares the resources for distribution.

SiliconForge, a microcontroller simulator designed around WebFront from the outset, is a first published application. The Game of Life used here is a smaller teaching example that lets us examine each mechanism separately.

We shall begin with the C++ simulation model and then build its interface. The same separation also allows an existing programme to be extended without changing its organisation.

The example programme

We shall use Conway’s Game of Life as our example. A grid of 32 × 32 cells follows two rules: a cell is born when it has three neighbours; a living cell survives when it has two or three. The edges of the grid wrap round.

Life.hpp calculates the next generation and returns a std::bitset<1024>. This computation has no dependency on a user interface library. We shall retain it when adding a window.

Building the examples

Building requires Git, CMake 3.31 or later, and a C++23 compiler. The first configuration downloads the C++ dependencies and therefore needs Internet access.

The following commands select version 0.7.0 and build the examples with the default options. They do not request a CEF download.

SYSTEM TERMINAL
git clone https://github.com/ambroise-leclerc/WebFront.git
cd WebFront
git checkout v0.7.0
mkdir build
cd build
cmake ..
cmake --build .

Running the simulation

From the build directory, run examples/WebFrontLifeConsole. With Visual Studio, use examples\Debug\WebFrontLifeConsole.exe. This initial version lets us examine the simulation before changing its presentation.

In an existing CMake project, add WebFront as a subproject and link the application target to WebFront::WebFront, as shown below.

CMAKE
add_subdirectory(path/to/WebFront)
add_executable(MyApp main.cpp)
target_link_libraries(MyApp PRIVATE WebFront::WebFront)
